text: Correction, 21 September 2026. The Platform pressure table included a sentence that described Palo Alto Networks and F5 as hyperscalers, for their acquisitions of Protect AI, and of CalypsoAI and SurePath AI. Neither Palo Alto Networks nor F5 is a hyperscaler, and all three targets are AI security companies, not cloud security companies. That sentence is withdrawn. Each of those three rows is dated to this approval and states only that the target was acquired by a platform vendor, with no claim about what happens to the product next. The row for Wiz, bought by Google, was correct as printed and is unchanged. Jesse Pike.

Correction, 20 September 2026. In the issue for the week ending 6 September 2026, two headlines gave a quarterly revenue figure as a full-year figure. Zscaler's revenue of $898.2 million and Palo Alto Networks' revenue of $3.41 billion are each for the fiscal fourth quarter ended 31 July 2026, not for fiscal year 2026. The growth rates and the recurring-revenue figures were stated correctly. The same issue described Palo Alto's 63 percent growth in Next-Generation Security recurring revenue as the fastest of the week's results; that figure is a company-defined segment and is not comparable with other companies' total revenue growth, so the comparison is withdrawn. The original text is unchanged in the record. Jesse Pike.

correctedReadings.correctedHeadline: Zscaler fiscal fourth-quarter revenue (quarter ended 31 July 2026) grows to $898.2M, +25% YoY; ARR grows to $3,771M, +25%
Palo Alto fiscal fourth-quarter revenue (quarter ended 31 July 2026) grows 34% to $3.41B; Next-Gen Security ARR $9.10B, +63%
correctedReadings.note: The original "why it matters" comparison, that this growth was the fastest among this week's public-issuer prints, is withdrawn. Next-Gen Security ARR is a company-defined segment and is not comparable with other companies' total revenue growth.
